issues.legal_issue: A real purchaser may seek a declaration of ownership when a court-sale certificate names another person fraudulently or without the real purchaser’s consent.
material_facts: The property was purchased at a court auction by a person acting as the claimant’s agent and power-of-attorney holder.
The expenses for the purchase and improvements were charged to the claimant’s account.
The agent’s name was entered in the sale certificate without the claimant’s knowledge or consent, and the claimant sought declaration and possession.
issues.conclusion: The bar on suits by beneficial owners under Section 66(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure did not prevent the claimant from seeking a declaration because the circumstances fell within the exception in Section 66(2).
issues.legal_principle: Section 66(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure generally bars a suit asserting that a court-auction purchaser bought on behalf of the plaintiff or someone through whom the plaintiff claims. Section 66(2), however, permits a suit for a declaration that the certified purchaser’s name was inserted fraudulently or without the real purchaser’s consent. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: suit_seeks_real_purchaser_declaration and claimant_is_real_purchaser and court_sale_certificate_names_another and (name_inserted_fraudulently or name_inserted_without_consent)

predicates.suit_seeks_real_purchaser_declaration: The claimant brought a suit seeking a declaration that the claimant, rather than the person named in the certificate, was the real purchaser.
predicates.claimant_is_real_purchaser: The claimant was the person for whose benefit the property was actually purchased.
predicates.court_sale_certificate_names_another: A certificate issued following a court sale named someone other than the real purchaser.
predicates.name_inserted_fraudulently: The other person’s name was inserted in the certificate by fraud.
predicates.name_inserted_without_consent: The other person’s name was inserted in the certificate without the real purchaser’s consent.

issues.definition: When a real purchaser seeks a declaration in a suit and a court-sale certificate names someone else fraudulently or without the purchaser’s consent, the declaration is permitted.

issues.legal_issue: An agent who acquires property for a principal while acting in a fiduciary capacity holds it for the principal, and the prohibition on benami claims does not bar the principal’s claim to title and possession in those circumstances.
material_facts: The purchaser acted as the claimant’s agent and power-of-attorney holder in managing the claimant’s properties.
The purchase and improvement expenses were met from the claimant’s funds.
The purchaser acquired the property for the claimant’s benefit but held the sale certificate in his own name without the claimant’s knowledge or consent.
The claimant sought declaration of title and recovery of possession.
issues.conclusion: The agent held the property in trust for the claimant; the benami prohibition did not prevent the claimant from obtaining declaration of title and possession.
issues.legal_principle: Section 88 of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, requires a person acting in a fiduciary capacity to hold a benefit obtained in that capacity for the person whose interests the fiduciary was bound to protect. Section 4(3)(b) of the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act excludes property held by a trustee or other person in a fiduciary capacity for another from the prohibition in Section 4. Section 7 of that Act did not repeal Section 88 of the Trusts Act. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: civil_property_claim and agent_acted_in_fiduciary_capacity and property_acquired_for_principal and principal_funds_used_for_acquisition

predicates.civil_property_claim: A claimant brought a civil claim seeking rights to property held in another person’s name.
predicates.agent_acted_in_fiduciary_capacity: The person who acquired the property was acting as an agent or in another fiduciary capacity for the claimant.
predicates.property_acquired_for_principal: The property was acquired for the benefit of the person whose interests the acquirer was bound to protect.
predicates.principal_funds_used_for_acquisition: The acquisition was funded by the person for whose benefit the property was acquired.

issues.definition: When a civil property claim concerns property acquired by a fiduciary for a principal using the principal’s funds, the principal is entitled to beneficial title and possession.
